A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AXE research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial restructuring and changed experimental scope.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet accuracy, WikiText2 perplexity, Pythia scaling experiments, and quantization ablations in Section 4 and Appendices C–D.

after.justification: v2 reports original hardware simulations, language-model quantization experiments, Llama3 zero-shot reasoning results, and appendix ablations.

M1.justification: AXE's soft thresholding, strict clipping, multi-stage accumulation, and memory-efficient GPFQ formulation are retained. However, Algorithm 1 changes the error-corrected assignment from temporary V_i in v1 to W_i in v2, which subsequently enters the error update. This locally changes the printed procedure; the unchanged surrounding recurrence leaves its intent and implementation unresolved.

E1.justification: v2 removes the ImageNet classification experiments, including their appendix results, while retaining WikiText2 language evaluation. It adds zero-shot evaluation on ARC-challenge, HellaSwag, PIQA, and Winogrande, plus vector-MAC simulations using random Gaussian inputs. This substantially changes the represented tasks and evaluation domains.

E2.justification: The language-model Pareto comparisons retain EP-init and naive bit-width manipulation. The new hardware analysis adds a comparison between the proposed accumulator-aware BOps model and a multiplication-only cost model in Figure 2. SmoothQuant and Hadamard incoherence processing are evaluated as preprocessing compositions, rather than entirely new competing quantizers.

E3.justification: v2 changes the stated activation scaling from per-tensor to per-token, adds Hadamard preprocessing to Pythia scaling, replaces FP32 references with FP16, extends scaling to 12B parameters, and drops 64-element tiles. It also adds SmolLM2/Llama3 configurations, hardware parameter sweeps, and averaged zero-shot accuracy. These are reported setting changes; retained numerical results do not establish that every experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds analyses of when addition costs dominate multiplication, whether BOps predicts simulated bit flips, and how bare, SmoothQuant, and Hadamard preprocessing affect Llama3 quantization. The existing rounding, error-correction, soft-constraint, and monolithic-accumulation ablations remain: v1 Tables 2–3 become v2 Tables 4–5 with unchanged ablation scores.

E5.justification: Section 3.1 and Figure 2 introduce correlation-based statistical reporting between predicted BOps and simulated bit flips, including trendlines and a reported 96% correlation. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for its experimental results.

E6.justification: v2 adds SmolLM2, Llama3 perplexity and reasoning, and hardware-simulation results, while removing ImageNet and 64-element-tile results. Pythia Table 1 is replaced under changed settings: for example, GPFQ with 128-element, 16-bit accumulation reports 15.2 perplexity for Pythia-6.9B in v1 versus 8.7 with Hadamard preprocessing in v2. This is not a same-setting gain. The retained older language Pareto and appendix ablation scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 introduces the formal accumulator-aware cost definition BOps = K(MN + (1-S)P) in Equation 5, incorporating sparsity and accumulator width. The central overflow bounds, multi-stage accumulator-width formula, and memory-efficient GPFQ equivalence theorem and proof are retained; the latter moves from Appendix B to Appendix A.

C1.justification: The title, abstract, and contributions narrow the empirical scope from image classification and language generation to language models. v2 additionally claims a Pareto-dominant power–quality trade-off and headline Llama3 performance retention. The original claims of accumulator-aware PTQ, overflow guarantees, and multi-stage accumulation remain.

C2.justification: v1 discusses an increasing gap from floating-point performance at larger Pythia sizes, identifies a 1B equilibrium, and leaves rotations for future work. Under its revised Hadamard setting, v2 instead emphasizes shrinking gaps through 12B and Llama3. It also adds interpretations connecting low operand precision to addition-cost dominance and SmolLM2 EP-init failures to round-to-zero quantization.

D1.justification: v2 adds Yosys/Arbolta simulation information, LightEval usage, SmoothQuant alpha = 0.4 selected through a grid search, and explicit 1% damping information for GPFQ. The MI210 hardware, Brevitas implementation, and language calibration sample and sequence-length details persist. The explicit final bias-correction description and ImageNet processing instructions disappear; omission alone does not establish that bias correction stopped being used.

R1.justification: The positioning shifts substantially toward low-power LLM inference, adding Amdahl's law, BOps/power literature, continuous batching, speculative decoding, and newer methods such as ISQ and Qronos. Much of the vision and broader deployment literature is removed. The relationship to A2Q/A2Q+ and the first accumulator-aware PTQ claim remain central.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten around LLMs and addition costs. v2 introduces a separate Motivation section, reorganizes the method exposition, moves both algorithms into the main text, restructures the experiments, and greatly condenses the conclusion. Appendix organization, title, author ordering, affiliations, and citation style also change.

P2.justification: v2 adds SmolLM2 accumulator/BOps plots, hardware bit-flip plots, and Llama3 tables. It merges the retained language panels from v1 Figures 1 and 3 into Figure 4, removes the vision panels and tables, relocates the algorithms, and redesigns several tables and the document layout. The accumulation diagram is retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens practical LLM evidence by testing rotation preprocessing left for future work in v1, adding downstream reasoning evaluation, and validating a hardware cost proxy. These gains trade away image-classification coverage and are tempered by new inconsistencies: Table 2 supports approximately 92% relative to FP16, whereas the abstract claims 98%, and Algorithm 1's in-place weight update conflicts with the retained recurrence. The added validation improves usefulness, but these reporting and reproducibility issues limit the net gain.
